1.name: Spellcasting
1.notes:
You learn to channel the magic of nature to cast Ranger spells.

Spell Slots. The Ranger Features table shows how many spell slots you have to cast level 1+ spells. You regain all expended spell slots when you finish a Long Rest.

Prepared Spells of Level 1+. You prepare a list of Ranger spells of level 1+ that you can cast with this feature. To start, choose two level 1 spells (Cure Wounds and Ensnaring Strike are recommended). Your number of prepared spells increases as you gain Ranger levels, as shown in the class table. Prepared spells must be of a level for which you have spell slots.
If another Ranger feature grants you spells that are always prepared, they don’t count against your number of prepared spells.

Changing Prepared Spells. When you finish a Long Rest, you may replace one prepared spell with another Ranger spell you can cast.

Spellcasting Ability. Wisdom is your spellcasting ability.

Spellcasting Focus. You can use a Druidic Focus as a Spellcasting Focus for your Ranger spells.

1.name: Favored Enemy
1.notes:
You always have the Hunter’s Mark spell prepared. You can cast it twice without expending a spell slot, regaining all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.
You gain additional free uses of Hunter’s Mark at higher levels, as shown in the class table.

1.name: Weapon Mastery
1.notes:
You can use the mastery properties of two kinds of weapons of your choice with which you have proficiency.
Whenever you finish a Long Rest, you may change the weapon types whose mastery properties you can use (for example, switching from Longbows and Shortswords to Scimitars and Longswords).

2.name: Deft Explorer
2.notes:
Your journeys have strengthened your survival skills.

Expertise. Choose one of your skill proficiencies with which you lack Expertise; you gain Expertise in that skill.

Languages. You learn two additional languages of your choice from the standard language lists.

2.name: Fighting Style
2.notes:
You gain a Fighting Style feat of your choice.

Alternatively, you may choose Druidic Warrior: you learn two Druid cantrips (Guidance and Starry Wisp are recommended). These cantrips count as Ranger spells for you, and Wisdom is your spellcasting ability for them. Whenever you gain a Ranger level, you may replace one of these cantrips with another Druid cantrip.

3.name: Frigid Explorer
3.notes:
You adapt to the harshest cold, gaining the following benefits:

Biting Cold. Your weapon attacks, Ranger spells, and Ranger features ignore Resistance to Cold damage.

Frost Resistance. You have Resistance to Cold damage.

Polar Strikes. When you hit a creature with a weapon attack, you deal an extra 1d4 Cold damage (once per turn). This increases to 1d6 at Ranger level 11.

3.name: Hunter's Rime
3.notes:
When you cast Hunter's Mark, you gain Temporary Hit Points equal to 1d10 + your Ranger level.

Additionally, a creature marked by your Hunter's Mark can't take the Disengage action.

3.name: Winter Walker Spells
3.notes:
You always have the following spells prepared at the listed Ranger levels:

3rd: Ice Knife
5th: Hold Person
9th: Remove Curse
13th: Ice Storm
17th: Cone of Cold

5.name: Extra Attack
5.notes: You can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.

6.name: Roving
6.notes: Your Speed increases by 10 feet while you aren’t wearing Heavy armor. You also gain a Climb Speed and a Swim Speed equal to your walking Speed.

traits.name: Draconic Ancestry
traits.notes: Your lineage stems from a dragon progenitor. Choose the kind of dragon from the Draconic Ancestors table. Your choice affects your Breath Weapon and Damage Resistance traits as well as your appearance.

traits.name: Breath Weapon
traits.notes: When you take the Attack action on your turn, you can replace one of your attacks with an exhalation of magical energy in either a 15-foot Cone or a 30-foot Line that is 5 feet wide (choose the shape each time). Each creature in that area must make a Dexterity saving throw (DC 8 plus your Constitution modifier and Proficiency Bonus). On a failed save, a creature takes 1d10 damage of the type determined by your Draconic Ancestry trait. On a successful save, a creature takes half as much damage. This damage increases by 1d10 when you reach character levels 5 (2d10), 11 (3d10), and 17 (4d10). You can use this Breath Weapon a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest

traits.name: Draconic Flight
traits.notes: When you reach character level 5, you can channel draconic magic to give yourself temporary flight. As a Bonus Action, you sprout spectral wings on your back that last for 10 minutes or until you retract the wings (no action required) or have the Incapacitated condition. During that time, you have a Fly Speed equal to your Speed. Your wings appear to be made of the same energy as your Breath Weapon. Once you use this trait, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

feats.notes: Enhanced Unarmed Strike. When you hit with your Unarmed Strike and deal damage, you can deal Bludgeoning damage equal to 1d4 plus your Strength modifier instead of the normal damage of an Unarmed Strike.Damage Rerolls. Whenever you roll a damage die for your Unarmed Strike, you can reroll the die if it rolls a 1, and you must use the new roll.Improvised Weaponry. You have proficiency with improvised weapons.Push. When you hit a creature with an Unarmed Strike as part of the Attack action on your turn, you can deal damage to the target and also push it 5 feet away from you. You can use this benefit only once per turn.
